DC. |date = 2023 |website = Plants of the World Online |publisher = Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date = 15 March 2023 }} }} [[File:Canavalia rosea foliage.jpg|thumb|Foliage]] '''''Canavalia rosea''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] of the genus ''[[Canavalia]]'' in the [[pea]] family of [[Fabaceae]], it has a [[pantropical]] and subtropical distribution in upper beaches, cliffs, and dunes.{{cite web |url=http://www.floridata.com/ref/c/cana_ros.cfm |first=Steve |last=Christman |title=#857 ''Canavalia rosea'' |work=Floridata |date=2004-01-14 |access-date=2010-12-04}} Common names include '''beach bean''', '''bay bean''', '''sea bean''', '''greater sea bean''', '''seaside jack-bean''', '''coastal jack-bean''', and '''MacKenzie bean'''. == Description == === Vine === Coastal jack-bean is a trailing, [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[vine]] that forms mats of foliage. Stems reach a length of more than {{convert|6|m|ft|abbr=on}} and {{convert|2.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} in thickness. Each compound leaf is made up of three leaflets {{convert|3.0|-|15.0|cm|in|abbr=on}} in diameter, which will fold themselves when exposed to hot sunlight. It is highly [[Halophyte|salt-tolerant]] and prefers [[sand]]y soils. [[File:Canavalia rosea at Ishigaki Island.jpg|center|thumb|''Canavalia rosea'' on the beaches of [[Ishigaki Island]]]] === Flowers and pods === The flowers are purplish pink and {{convert|2.5|-|5.1|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, they hang upside down from long stalks and produce a sweet smell. The flat pods are straight or a little curved, {{convert|6.0|-|15.2|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, their skin becoming prominently ridged as they mature. Each pod has between 2–10 brown seeds. The seeds are buoyant so they can be [[Drift seed|distributed]] by ocean currents. The plant seems to contain [[L-Betonicine]].{{Citation needed|date=June 2019}} The Canavalia rosea plant fruits and blooms all year long[https://www.fnps.org/plant/canavalia-rosea]. File:Canavalia rosea MHNT.BOT.2016.24.55.jpg|''C. rosea'' pods and seeds == Uses == Young seeds and pods are edible, especially after boiling. The flowers can be made into a spice.
